{"commits":[{"authoredDate":"2026-09-17T17:04:29Z","authors":[{"email":"jerimiah797@gmail.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE1ODQyODI=","login":"jerimiah797","name":"Jerimiah Ham"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-17T17:04:29Z","messageBody":"Under Xcode 27 every idb HID command failed: the patched companion
looked for SimulatorKit where Xcode 26 kept it (#222). idb is the
fallback when sim-bridge cannot run, so on Xcode 27 there was none.

quern-dev/idb idb-companion-v2 (fix/xcode27-simulatorkit @ a9daf33d)
finds SimulatorKit in either location, and is built with Xcode 27.
Setup now installs v2 and records the installed release in
~/.quern/bin/idb_companion.release. The marker is cleared before an
install and written only once the new binary is in place. v1 wrote no
marker, so an install without one is read as v1.

check_idb_companion reports an install that is not the current release
as a fixable warning, and setup offers to replace it on both paths. That
includes Apple Silicon machines with Xcode 26+, where setup otherwise
skips idb entirely. An install left there by an older setup is still
the fallback, and it cannot work under Xcode 27. A declined or failed
update is reported as such, rather than as "not required".

docs/idb-companion-distribution.md now records both releases and how to
build one. That wasn't written down before, and v2 needed Homebrew
build tools, an arm64 thin and an ad-hoc re-sign to match v1's layout.

Verified:
- The published tarball (sha256 6585ceba...) installs through
  _install_patched_companion from the real URL, and the check reports
  OK.
- On this machine, a real v1 install reported as outdated. The update
  path replaced it, and the stock IdbBackend then swiped an iOS 18.6
  simulator under Xcode 27 (223pt for a 233pt, 1.0s drag). Before the
  update the same call failed.
- The staged v2 bundle also tapped, typed and ran describe-all
  (32 elements).
- 7 mutants of the new setup code, all killed. Unit suite 2597.","messageHeadline":"Install idb-companion-v2, and replace v1 wherever it is found","oid":"f1942b207bee2b82065f6a26692845989f1f2626"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-17T17:45:41Z","authors":[{"email":"jerimiah797@gmail.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE1ODQyODI=","login":"jerimiah797","name":"Jerimiah Ham"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-17T17:45:41Z","messageBody":"dev-34's review (PR comment 5718734042) found two medium problems and
six low ones.

- A marker that isn't UTF-8 raised UnicodeDecodeError, a ValueError,
  and crashed the check, companion_is_outdated and setup. The read now
  catches (OSError, ValueError).
- The source-text test of run_setup let two broken wirings pass: an
  offer computed after report.add and thrown away, and an offer
  commented out. The companion step is now _setup_idb_companion(), and
  its tests drive it for both paths (accepted, declined, failed, and
  current-with-sim-bridge). Only the two report.add calls are still
  checked in the source.
- An update used to extract straight over the install. It now
  downloads and extracts into a staging directory under ~/.quern/bin.
  It checks the payload has both bin/idb_companion and Frameworks/,
  then swaps Frameworks/ wholesale (restoring the old one if the swap
  fails) and replaces the binary atomically. A full disk can no longer
  leave v1 beside half of v2, and files only v1 had (95 nested ones)
  are gone.
- The marker is cleared at the swap, not before the download. A failed
  re-download no longer makes a current install read as v1. A marker
  path that is a directory is a reported failure, not a crash. A marker
  that can't be written after a successful swap no longer turns into
  "Update failed".
- "Outdated" means older: a marker naming a newer release, left by a
  later quern before a rollback, is not offered a downgrade. A marker
  naming no release number is still outdated.
- The docs and changelog note the macOS 12 minimum and the staging
  swap. The v2 release notes now say idb xctest is probably still
  broken under Xcode 27, where XCTAutomationSupport also moved.

17 mutants of the new code, all killed. That includes the four the

From dev-34's re-review (PR comment 5720462720):

- `_setup_idb_companion` kept two paths from the inline code that no
  test pinned: removing the MISSING branch, or the "installed (system"
  branch, survived the suite. MISSING is the main path on a fresh
  machine. Four stub cases cover both now, including a declined offer.
- The binary moves last, and a failure there left the new frameworks
  beside the old binary -- with the retired tree already deleted. It
  now puts both back.
- If the frameworks rollback itself fails there are no frameworks at
  all. That recovers on the next setup, because the marker was already
  cleared, and the comment now says so.
- Staging directories only survive a kill -9, and each is ~17MB, so
  stale ones are cleared before a new install rather than accumulating.

# Conflicts:
#	CHANGELOG.md","messageHeadline":"Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into fix/idb-companion-xco…","oid":"aa86385d768f2a139507a723c76dc834ae56b500"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-19T23:32:43Z","authors":[{"email":"jerimiah797@gmail.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE1ODQyODI=","login":"jerimiah797","name":"Jerimiah Ham"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-19T23:32:43Z","messageBody":"Intel is exactly where setup reaches this code: _sim_bridge_supported()
is False there, so run_setup takes the sim_bridge=False branch that
offers the patched download. The published asset is arm64-only, and
IdbBackend prefers ~/.quern/bin/idb_companion over the system one -- so
accepting the offer would shadow a working Homebrew companion with a
binary that cannot execute.

The refusal goes in _install_patched_companion, which every caller goes
through, and the two prompts are suppressed as well: asking a question
whose answer cannot be honoured and then reporting the refusal as
'Download failed' describes the wrong problem. companion_is_outdated
answers False there too, since there is nothing to update to.

The test helpers now pin _is_apple_silicon. They did not need to before,
and CI's Linux runners report x86_64 -- so without that every existing
install test would have started exercising the refusal path instead.

One of the four new tests passed against the mutant on the first pass:
it stubbed the download to raise, the installer caught that and returned
False, and the assertion on the return value held whether it refused up
front or tried and fell over. It asserts on what was attempted now.

Also: the CHANGELOG claimed every interrupted update leaves the previous
install working, which is stronger than the code. An interruption during
the swap can leave the tree half replaced; what is guaranteed is that it
reads as outdated rather than current. And the docs' install example was
a pre-implementation sketch -- v1, extract-over-destination, skip if
present, no marker -- replaced by what the implementation actually does.","messageHeadline":"Do not offer the arm64 companion on an Intel Mac","oid":"51f8cc3a9a19565967e3f3e3b4c4d704a125c234"}]}
